title: Design a URL shortener
prompt: Design the read path for a URL shortener (e.g. bit.ly). Reads (redirects) dominate writes ~100:1. Drag the components onto the canvas and connect them to show how a redirect request flows from the user to a stored mapping — and how you keep p99 redirect latency low under heavy read load.

criteria.label: Request originates from a client
criteria.metWhy: Good — the design starts from the client/user issuing the redirect request.
criteria.why: Add a User/Client component so the request path has a clear origin.

criteria.label: Traffic enters through a load balancer or API gateway
criteria.metWhy: Traffic is spread across instances via a load balancer / gateway / edge — no single hot box.
criteria.why: Put a Load Balancer, API Gateway, or CDN in front so reads fan out across many instances.

criteria.label: A stateless service tier handles the lookup
criteria.metWhy: A stateless service resolves short codes — easy to scale horizontally.
criteria.why: Add a Server/Service tier that performs the short-code lookup; keep it stateless so you can add replicas.

criteria.label: Mappings are kept in a durable datastore
criteria.metWhy: Short-code → long-URL mappings live in a durable store, the source of truth.
criteria.why: Add a Database to durably store the short-code → long-URL mappings.

criteria.label: Hot redirects are served from a cache
criteria.metWhy: A cache absorbs the 100:1 read skew so most redirects never touch the database.
criteria.why: Reads dominate ~100:1 — add a Cache so popular short codes are served from memory, not the DB.

criteria.label: The service reads through the cache
criteria.metWhy: The service is wired to the cache — the redirect read path actually uses it.
criteria.why: Connect your Service to the Cache so the lookup checks cache first (a cache nobody is wired to does nothing).

criteria.label: The service falls back to the datastore
criteria.metWhy: On a cache miss the service falls back to the database — a complete read path.
criteria.why: Connect your Service to the Database so a cache miss can fall back to the source of truth.

criteria.label: The design has enough moving parts to be a real architecture
criteria.metWhy: The design has the core building blocks of a real read path.
criteria.why: Sketch at least the core pieces (client, entry point, service, store) before submitting.
